text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- International High Representative to Bosnia, Carl Bildt said on Monday that this week's Paris peace conference will discuss next spring's municipal elections, the work of common institutions and other issues related to Bosnia.

- Although the minimum technical requirements are in place for the operation of the railway from Sarajevo to Croatian port of Ploce, the line is at a standstill, a Bosnian Federation official tells the newspaper on Tuesday.

- According to the Bosnian Statistics Company, Bosnian pensioners last received pensions only for October. They still have not received their pensions for May, June, July, August or September this year. The average pension for October was 9,758 Bosnian Dinars (97.8 DEM). The company also says Bosnia's inflation rate for the first nine months of the year was 1,007 percent.
- The number of unemployed people in Bosnia has reached 850,000 and is at a critical stage, the state Statistics Company says in its survey.

- An Italian company has donated 300,000 DEM worth of equipment for repairs of the electrical network to the Bosnian electricity company Elektroprivreda, the company's general menager said. He added that Italy is the first country that Bosnia has started to export electrical energy to.
- Swiss and Bosnian government officials signed a 9.5 million DEM loan in Sarajevo on Tuesday to help rebuild a hydro-electric dam in Bosnian town of Jablanica.
